blocks.text: NUS' main campus since 1980, the sprawling 150-hectare Kent Ridge Campus hosts most of the University's academic, research and administrative facilities. It is also a bustling hub of student life, with student residences, sports facilities and venues for arts and cultural activities.

University Town (UTown) – an extension of the Kent Ridge Campus – offers a unique residential college experience, as well as a host of educational and recreational spaces for interaction, peer learning and personal development. UTown is also home to Yale-NUS College, Singapore's first liberal arts college with a full residential programme.

The Bukit Timah Campus houses the Faculty of Law and the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy. The colonial style buildings date back to 1928 when NUS' predecessor institution, Raffles College, was established.
